claims.quote: (3) A direction that the defendant file with the court a written pleading in response to the complaint within 30 days after summons is served on the defendant.
claims.note: The draft omits the service trigger. Subdivision (a) also qualifies the summons requirements with “Except as otherwise required by statute”.

claims.claim: Talking with the collector or their lawyer does not pause the deadline.
claims.note: The cited section specifies what the summons must say, not whether a call affects the deadline.

claims.claim: Do not rely on a promise of more time unless it is in writing.
claims.note: No source addresses oral or written extension promises.

claims.claim: A written promise must also be confirmed with the court clerk or a lawyer before relying on it.
claims.note: The section mentions seeking attorney advice but gives no confirmation procedure involving a clerk or lawyer.

flags.text: No extension or tolling authority is provided for the central answer.
“Any time before a response is filed” does not distinguish time before service from time after the response deadline.
“Do not rely” directs the reader to use an unsupported writing-and-confirmation test.

A reader might treat a confirmed written promise as sufficient and delay filing. The summons warns that default will be entered upon the plaintiff’s application if the defendant does not respond as directed.

result.summary: The source supports the summons’s 30-day filing direction after service. It does not establish the effect of a call or how an extension can be verified.
